beats.content:
Hard-coding `#1e1e1e` everywhere means editing every copy when the colour changes. Instead, point styles at the presets you registered in `settings`. theme.json has its own syntax for that:

```text
var:preset|{feature}|{slug}
```

So your `base` colour is `var:preset|color|base`:

```json
"styles": {
  "color": {
    "background": "var:preset|color|base",
    "text": "var:preset|color|contrast"
  }
}
```

Behind the scenes, WordPress turns each preset into a CSS custom property, such as `--wp--preset--color--base`. In theme.json, use the `var:preset|…` form, because it shows up correctly in the Styles interface. Save the `var(--wp--preset--color--base)` form for when you're writing actual CSS.

The same idea works beyond colour. The finished theme at the end of this path uses two more:

- **A font preset.** Register a font stack in `settings.typography.fontFamilies` (each entry has a `name`, a `slug` and a `fontFamily`), then apply it with `var:preset|font-family|{slug}` in `styles.typography.fontFamily`. A system stack such as `system-ui, sans-serif` needs no font files.
- **Root padding.** `styles.spacing.padding` sets the padding around the whole site. Declare `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` separately and turn on `settings.useRootPaddingAwareAlignments`, so full-width blocks reach the screen edges while their content keeps that padding.
beats.goal: Use your presets instead of hex codes.
beats.question: Why does referencing a preset make a later redesign easier?

checks.message: theme.json must be valid JSON once your styles are in. styles goes next to settings, separated by a comma.
Your palette needs an accent entry (name, slug accent and a hex color), and your links need to use it. Keep version 3 in theme.json.
The site background goes in a color object directly under styles. Point it at the base preset with the var:preset syntax.
The text colour sits next to the background colour. Use the contrast preset.
Links are an element, so they go under styles.elements, then link, then color. Use the accent preset.

checkpoint.question: Add a top-level styles section to your theme.json. Set the site background to your base colour, the text to your contrast colour, and every link to your accent colour. Use preset references, not hex codes.
checkpoint.rubric: theme.json has styles.color.background "var:preset|color|base", styles.color.text "var:preset|color|contrast" and styles.elements.link.color.text "var:preset|color|accent", with version 3.
